```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(Seurat)
library(Signac)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(GenomeInfoDb)
library(ggplot2)
library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86) # For genome annotations
```

## 1. Load Annotated Multiome Object
First, we load the saved multiome object containing our RNA/ATAC data, WNN clusters, and scType cell annotations.
```{r load_data}
# Path to the annotated RDS object saved from the previous step
ATAC_gang <- readRDS("outputs/Multiome_WNN_scType_Annotated.rds")

# Verify the object
ATAC_gang
```

## 2. MACS2 Execution Details (External via Cluster)
MACS2 was run manually on the cluster via Singularity using the fragments file:
```bash
# 1. Clean fragment file headers:
# echo 'zgrep -v "^#" /path/to/fragments.tsv.gz > /path/to/clean_fragments.bed' | run_cluster.pl -cpu=1

# 2. Call peaks with MACS2:
# echo 'run_singularity.sh macs2_macs3.sif macs2 callpeak \
#   -t /data-pure/workspace/fdervis/Ganglioglioma/Multiome/MACS2_peakCalling/clean_fragments.bed \
#   -f BED --nomodel --shift -75 --extsize 150 \
#   --outdir /data-pure/workspace/fdervis/Ganglioglioma/Multiome/MACS2_peakCalling \
#   -n ganglioglioma_peaks_GG001AC -g hs' | run_cluster.pl -cpu=4
```

## 3. Import MACS2 Peaks & Build Fixed-Width Consensus Peakset

### Proposition 2: Filter by Statistical Significance (q-value)
MACS2 narrowPeak column 9 contains `-log10(q-value)`. Filtering at `neg_log10qvalue >= 2` corresponds to FDR $q \le 0.01$ (1% FDR), discarding low-confidence marginal noise before fragment quantification.

### Proposition 1: Fixed-Width 501 bp Summit-Centered Peaks (Corces et al. 2018 Standard)
* **The Problem:** Raw MACS2 peaks vary in length (from 150 bp to multiple kilobases). When counting reads into variable-width peaks, wider regions capture more counts simply because of their larger genomic span, confounding peak width with true biological accessibility.
* **The Solution:** Centering a fixed 501 bp window ($\pm 250\text{ bp}$) on the exact MACS2 peak summit standardizes all features to equal genomic size. Applying iterative overlap removal eliminates redundant summits while keeping the most statistically significant regulatory center.

### Proposition 3 (TODO FOR LATER ITERATION): Per-Cluster Pseudobulk Peak Calling
* **Context & Rationale:** Currently, peaks were called on bulk fragments pooled across all cells. While this generates a reliable core peakset, bulk peak calling is dominated by high-abundance populations (e.g., astrocytic tumor cells) and under-represents rare sub-populations (e.g., tumor-associated microglia, pericytes, rare neuronal subtypes).
* **Roadmap / TODO:** In a future iteration, we can split fragment reads by `sctype_classification` cluster barcodes, run MACS2 independently on each pseudobulk subpopulation, and merge them using iterative overlap removal into a comprehensive consensus peakset.

```{r import_and_standardize_macs2_peaks}
# Path to the MACS2 narrowPeak file on the cluster
macs2_peak_path <- "/data-pure/workspace/fdervis/Ganglioglioma/Multiome/MACS2_peakCalling/ganglioglioma_peaks_GG001AC_peaks.narrowPeak"

# Read narrowPeak file (standard BED6+4 format from MACS2)
peaks_df <- read.table(
  file = macs2_peak_path,
  col.names = c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "score", "strand", 
                "fold_change", "neg_log10pvalue", "neg_log10qvalue", "relative_summit_pos")
)

cat("Total raw peaks identified by MACS2:", nrow(peaks_df), "\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Proposition 2: Filter by Statistical Significance (q <= 0.01, neg_log10qvalue >= 2)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
qval_threshold <- 2  # -log10(0.01) = 2
peaks_filtered_df <- peaks_df[peaks_df$neg_log10qvalue >= qval_threshold, ]
cat("Peaks passing q-value threshold (q <= 0.01):", nrow(peaks_filtered_df), "\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Proposition 1: Standardize to Fixed-Width 501 bp Centered on Peak Summits
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Absolute 1-based summit position: start (0-based) + relative_summit_pos + 1
summit_1based <- peaks_filtered_df$start + peaks_filtered_df$relative_summit_pos + 1

# Create summit GRanges
summits_gr <- GRanges(
  seqnames = peaks_filtered_df$chr,
  ranges = IRanges(start = summit_1based, width = 1),
  name = peaks_filtered_df$name,
  score = peaks_filtered_df$score,
  neg_log10qvalue = peaks_filtered_df$neg_log10qvalue,
  fold_change = peaks_filtered_df$fold_change
)

# Standardize to 501 bp fixed-width window centered on summit (+/- 250 bp)
peaks_fixed <- resize(summits_gr, width = 501, fix = "center")

# Iterative Overlap Removal (Corces et al. 2018):
# Order peaks by statistical significance descending
peaks_sorted <- peaks_fixed[order(peaks_fixed$neg_log10qvalue, decreasing = TRUE)]

# Greedy iterative non-overlapping selection: keep top summit when 501bp windows overlap
overlaps <- findOverlaps(peaks_sorted, peaks_sorted)
query_hits <- queryHits(overlaps)
subject_hits <- subjectHits(overlaps)

# Identify non-self overlaps where a higher-ranked peak (lower index) overlaps a lower-ranked peak
non_self <- query_hits < subject_hits
keep_peaks <- rep(TRUE, length(peaks_sorted))
if (any(non_self)) {
  drop_idx <- unique(subject_hits[non_self])
  keep_peaks[drop_idx] <- FALSE
}

peaks <- peaks_sorted[keep_peaks]
cat("Consensus non-overlapping 501 bp fixed-width peaks retained:", length(peaks), "\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Genomic Range Cleaning (Standard Chromosomes & ENCODE Blacklist)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
seqlevelsStyle(peaks) <- "UCSC"

# Filter out non-standard chromosomes (scaffolds / unplaced contigs)
peaks <- keepStandardChromosomes(peaks, pruning.mode = "coarse")

# Filter out ENCODE blacklist regions (artefactual genomic regions)
peaks <- subsetByOverlaps(x = peaks, ranges = blacklist_hg38_unified, invert = TRUE)

cat("Final high-confidence, blacklist-filtered 501 bp peaks for quantification:", length(peaks), "\n")
```

## 4. Quantify Fragments Against MACS2 Peaks
Now that we have high-confidence MACS2 peaks, we quantify the ATAC fragment counts across all cells for this new peak set.
```{r quantify_fragments}
# Ensure the default assay is ATAC (Multiome_WNN_scType_Annotated.rds had DefaultAssay set to RNA)
DefaultAssay(ATAC_gang) <- "ATAC"

# Extract fragment object from the ATAC ChromatinAssay (or fallback to fragment file path if needed)
frag_path <- "/data-pure/sequencing/ngs/NGS2026_10893/HG38/count/cellranger/GG001AC/atac_fragments.tsv.gz"
atac_fragments <- Fragments(ATAC_gang[["ATAC"]])
if (length(atac_fragments) == 0) {
  atac_fragments <- CreateFragmentObject(path = frag_path, cells = colnames(ATAC_gang))
}

# Quantify fragments in each cell for the MACS2 peak set
macs2_counts <- FeatureMatrix(
  fragments = atac_fragments,
  features = peaks,
  cells = colnames(ATAC_gang)
)

# Retrieve existing gene annotations from the ATAC ChromatinAssay
annotations <- Annotation(ATAC_gang[["ATAC"]])

# Create a new Chromatin Assay with the MACS2 peak counts
new_atac_assay <- CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts = macs2_counts,
  fragments = atac_fragments,
  annotation = annotations,
  genome = "hg38"
)

# Replace the old Cell Ranger ATAC assay with the high-resolution MACS2 assay
ATAC_gang[["ATAC"]] <- new_atac_assay
DefaultAssay(ATAC_gang) <- "ATAC"

cat("New ATAC assay successfully created and assigned as default assay.\n")
```

## 5. Dimensionality Reduction on MACS2 Peaks
We recompute TF-IDF normalization, feature selection, and SVD (LSI) on the refined peak set.
```{r lsi_dimreduc}
# TF-IDF and SVD
ATAC_gang <- RunTFIDF(ATAC_gang)
ATAC_gang <- FindTopFeatures(ATAC_gang, min.cutoff = "q0")
ATAC_gang <- RunSVD(ATAC_gang)

# Run UMAP on the new MACS2 LSI reduction (excluding 1st component correlated with depth)
ATAC_gang <- RunUMAP(
  ATAC_gang,
  reduction = "lsi",
  dims = 2:50,
  reduction.name = "umap.atac.macs2",
  reduction.key = "atacMACS2UMAP_"
)

# Visualize the new ATAC UMAP colored by scType classification
DimPlot(
  ATAC_gang,
  reduction = "umap.atac.macs2",
  group.by = "sctype_classification",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE,
  label.size = 2.5
) + ggtitle("MACS2 ATAC UMAP by Cell Type")
```

## 6. (Optional) Recompute Multimodal WNN with MACS2 Peaks
You can also re-run Weighted Nearest Neighbors (WNN) using the RNA PCA and the new MACS2 LSI reduction.
```{r recompute_wnn}
ATAC_gang <- FindMultiModalNeighbors(
  ATAC_gang,
  reduction.list = list("pca", "lsi"),
  dims.list = list(1:50, 2:50)
)

ATAC_gang <- RunUMAP(
  ATAC_gang,
  nn.name = "weighted.nn",
  reduction.name = "wnn.umap.macs2",
  reduction.key = "wnnMACS2UMAP_"
)

# Plot updated WNN UMAP
DimPlot(
  ATAC_gang,
  reduction = "wnn.umap.macs2",
  group.by = "sctype_classification",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE,
  label.size = 2.5
) + ggtitle("Refined WNN (RNA + MACS2 ATAC)")
```

## 7. Save Updated Multiome Object
Save the final multiome object containing the MACS2 peaks and updated embeddings.
```{r save_object}
saveRDS(ATAC_gang, file = "Multiome_MACS2_Peaks.rds")
cat("Object saved as Multiome_MACS2_Peaks.rds\n")
```
